newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber ends down, trade unmoved by Deng.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber ends down, trade unmoved by Deng.

text.p: Rubber futures closed lower on Thursday in moderate trade while the trade reacted with a shrug to the death of Chinese paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, dealers said.
"Forget about Deng. It doesn't affect the market at all. It's a very miserable, dead market today," a dealer for a Japanese rubber trading firm said.

Traders said there was some moderate buying for RSS3 rubber, especially for forward supplies of RSS3 rubber. Volume in RSS1 and TSR20 rubber was thin, the dealers added. "It was dull. Lower prices in Tokyo pushed the market down," one trader said.
Tokyo's benchmark July contract slipped two yen to settle at 155.8 yen. Total volume of RSS3 rubber traded reached over 4,000 tonnes against about 2,000 tonnes each for RSS1 and TSR20 rubber.
At around 0945 GMT, April RSS3 was seen at 121.00-122.00 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 123.00 cents.
June RSS1 was seen at 173.00-175.00 Singapore cents (US$1.22-$1.23) a kg from the previous 175.50 cents.
March TSR20 was seen at 166.50-168.50 Singapore cents (US$1.17-$1.19) a kg against 168.75 cents.
